info.desc: The debut album by Kings of Leon takes its name from a Pentecostal Bible verse. The album was recorded in Malibu and Nashville with Ethan Johns. The album was critically acclaimed and a hit in the UK and Ireland, but failed to make an impact elsewhere in the world. It has since sold 1 million copies. "Molly's Chambers," "Wasted Time" and "California Waiting" were all released as singles. "Spiral Staircase" featured on the PS3 game MotorStorm. "Holy Roller Novocaine" was featured in the movie Talladega Nights: The Ballad of Ricky Bobby. "Red Morning Light" was also featured on a Ford .

podcast.body: This was Kings of Leon's first full-length album, released approximately six to eight months after their debut EP. The title was inspired by a phrase found in the back of their preacher father's Bible, specifically from an illustration of the "tree of Moses' life" detailing stages like "Youth and Young Manhood". This album was particularly successful in the UK and Europe. It included material from their first EP, with some songs appearing as-is and others re-recorded, notably featuring "Molly's Chambers". "Youth and Young Manhood was the album that I guess really caught on the UK and Europe and then kind of went from there."
